title: Struckd Alternative on iPad: Build 2D Games with hyperPad
summary: Compare Struckd and hyperPad by creative control, visual logic, asset workflow, project structure, and the path from prototype to published iOS game.
body_markdown:
*Reviewed October 7, 2026. Struckd facts refer to[the current official Struckd information](https://struckd.com/) available on that date. Plans, device support, and publishing terms can change.*


If you want to create a 2D game with visual logic on iPad, **hyperPad is the option to take** . Its editor was designed around Scenes, Objects, Graphics, Attributes, and connected Behaviors. You can build, test, and improve the game on the same device instead of assembling a separate coding toolchain.


hyperPad is iPad-first. The current App Store listing also makes the paid app available on compatible Apple-silicon Macs, including M1 and later, and its release notes document macOS editor fixes. The App Store listing provides the current compatibility details for each device.


## hyperPad vs Struckd: quick comparison


Decision factor hyperPad Struckd


Best fit **Complete visual 2D game creation on iPad and compatible Apple-silicon Macs** quick 3D game assembly


Where you create **Native, iPad-first editor** mobile and desktop creation platform


How logic works **Connected visual Behaviors for events, actions, conditions, input, and state** template and asset-led tools


Game systems **Scenes, Objects, Attributes, physics, UI, animation, audio, particles, shaders, and reusable Prefabs** Tools shaped around its library-led workflow


Test and iterate **Run the Project in the editor, adjust a Behavior, and test again** Testing follows its library-led workflow


Community feedback **Share through the hyperPad Hub and continue the conversation in the Forum** Uses its own community or distribution options


Starting point **Free, ad-free Starter with one editable Project** Refer to the dated official source above


Path forward **Grow the Project, share it, and use Xcode Export for the iOS release workflow** Publishing follows its current plan and platform workflow


## Why hyperPad is the stronger visual-coding choice


### Build game logic without hiding the real concepts


Behaviors represent events, actions, conditions, loops, values, input, and state. A collision can increase a score Attribute, play audio, remove an Object, and test a win condition. You see the order of the logic and can debug each connection.


The[Behavior Interface Overview](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/behavior-interface-overview) explains the editor.[Behavior Bundles](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/behavior-bundle) let you organize connected logic and control execution order.


### Work with complete game systems


hyperPad is not limited to a lesson or a fixed template. A Project can include:


- multiple Scenes and overlays
- physics and collision systems
- UI, labels, buttons, health, and score
- animation, particles, shaders, audio, and music
- arrays, dictionaries, timers, loops, and reusable logic
- Prefabs and Templates shared across Scenes
- touch, keyboard, mouse, trackpad, tilt, and controller input
- networking and multiplayer Behaviors
- imported graphics, fonts, animations, music, and sound effects


That range lets a beginner start with one mechanic while giving an experienced creator room to build a deeper prototype.


### Create on iPad or a compatible Apple-silicon Mac


On iPad, the editor supports touch, Apple Pencil, keyboard, mouse, and trackpad workflows. On a compatible M1-or-later Mac, the same App Store app can support a larger-screen keyboard and pointer workflow. hyperPad remains an iPad-first product, so this is one creation system rather than separate tablet and desktop editors.


### Test immediately and improve with feedback


You can run the Project from the editor, change one Behavior, and test again. Paid hyperPad can publish projects to the hyperPad Hub for community feedback. The[Forum](https://www.hyperpad.com/forum) and[documentation](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation) provide help as the project grows.


### Start free without a subscription


[hyperPad Starter](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6737631128?pt=467885&ct=blog_struckd_comparison&mt=8) is free, ad-free, and includes one editable Project. Starter is for building and testing. Upgrade when you need more Projects, Hub sharing, or Xcode Export.


When the game is ready for release, paid hyperPad provides Xcode Export for Apple’s signing and App Store submission workflow.


## What Struckd currently offers


- Struckd centers on accessible game creation and community play.
- Its workflow emphasizes ready-made elements and rapid assembly.
- Check its current official listing for device and publishing availability.


For creators comparing the practical path from idea to playable 2D game, hyperPad brings the editor, visual logic, assets, testing, project structure, and community feedback into one Apple-device workflow.


## A five-minute way to compare them


Build the same small mechanic in both tools:


1. Add a player and a collectable.
2. Move the player with touch or keyboard input.
3. Detect the collision.
4. Add one to a score.
5. Remove the collectable and show a win state.


In hyperPad, that test uses Objects, an Attribute, and connected Behaviors. It demonstrates the same programming concepts used in larger games without requiring syntax before you can see the idea work.


## The decision for visual game creators


Choose **hyperPad** when you want to turn an idea into a playable 2D game through visual coding on iPad or a compatible Apple-silicon Mac. You get a purpose-built game editor, immediate testing, reusable logic, custom assets, community feedback, and an iOS export path in one workflow.


That makes the decision especially clear for iPad owners, teachers, students, artists, designers, and developers who want to prototype without building a separate code toolchain.


## Common questions


### Is hyperPad only for beginners?


No. Beginners can connect their first event and action without syntax, while advanced creators can build reusable systems with Prefabs, arrays, dictionaries, physics, networking, custom input, shaders, and complex state.


### Does hyperPad work on Mac?


The current paid-app listing is available for compatible Apple-silicon Macs, including M1 and later. The product remains designed around its iPad-first editor. Confirm compatibility in the App Store on the Mac you plan to use.


### Where should I begin?


Follow[How to Use hyperPad](https://www.hyperpad.com/blog/how-to-use-hyperpad) , then build one mechanic in Starter before expanding the Project.


Choose the workflow that fits the Project you want to finish. Test one representative mechanic before committing to a larger build, then judge the tool by how clearly you can create, test, and revise it.
